name: Arachim (Torah Valuations)
notes: Fixed Torah valuations by age and sex (Lev. 27:3-7); who can vow/be valuated; tumtum, androginus, minor, deaf-mute in context of valuations; age categories (1 month-5, 5-20, 20-60, 60+)

name: Arachim vs. Erech — Valuation vs. Assessment Distinction
notes: Distinction between fixed Torah valuation (erech) and market-value assessment (damim); cases where one is stricter/more lenient than the other

name: Affordability in Valuations (Yashot haYad)
notes: The priest's ability to reduce valuation payment for destitute person; minimum of one sela; maximum of fifty sela; whose means determine the amount

name: Valuation of Limbs
notes: Whether one can vow the valuation of a limb; items upon which the soul depends trigger full valuation; vow of one's weight

name: Cherem (Dedication to Priests or Temple)
notes: Detailed laws of cherem: dedicating property, animals, or persons; whether cherem goes to priests or Temple treasury; limits on what may be dedicated; priests and Levites and cherem

name: Sdeh Achuzah — Ancestral Field Consecration Laws
notes: Detailed laws: redemption at 50 shekels per beit kor; counting years to Jubilee; crevices and boulders; who may redeem; one-fifth addition for owner; what happens if not redeemed by Jubilee; Levite cities fields

name: Sdeh Miknah — Purchased Field Consecration Laws
notes: Laws of consecrating a purchased field: redemption at market value; does not go to priests at Jubilee; distinction from ancestral field; case where son purchased from father

name: Batei Arei Chomah — Houses in Walled Cities
notes: Detailed laws: 12-month redemption window; becomes permanent after one year; Hillel's enactment of chamber for deposit; definition of walled city (from Joshua's era); houses vs. fields within walls; Levite city houses

name: Proclamation of Consecrated Property Sale (Hakrazah)
notes: Announcing the sale of consecrated property or orphan's property for 30 or 60 days morning and evening to maximize price; bidding procedures; reneging on bids

name: Repossession of Property for Valuations and Hekdesh
notes: Court repossession of property to pay valuations; what the treasurer leaves for the obligated person (30 days food, 12 months clothing, tools of trade); phylacteries; wife and children's garments

name: Conflict Between Hekdesh and Ketubah/Creditor Claims
notes: When one consecrates property that has liens for ketubah or creditor; collusion prevention; vow of benefit to prevent remarriage after divorce

name: Forewarned Ox Killing a Canaanite Slave
notes: Fixed payment of 30 sela regardless of slave's value; contrast with killing a freeman; injury payment based on actual damage

name: Status of Condemned Person in Valuations and Vows
notes: Whether a moribund person or one sentenced to death can be subject to vows of assessment or valuation; dispute between Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya and Rabbi Yosi

name: Execution of a Pregnant Woman
notes: Court does not wait for pregnant condemned woman to give birth; but if she sat on the birthing chair, execution is delayed; distinction from benefit of her hair after death

name: Laws of Levite Cities
notes: Levites may always redeem their fields and houses; 2000 cubits surrounding cities; division into empty lots and fields; prohibition on converting field to empty lot or vice versa; Levite inheritance from Israelite

name: Temple Trumpet Blasts (Teki'ot HaMikdash)
notes: Minimum 21 and maximum 48 trumpet blasts daily; occasions for extra blasts; Friday of Sukkot with water libation; signals for gates, offerings, and Shabbat

name: Levite Musicians in the Temple
notes: Minimum and maximum numbers of lyres, flutes, harps; 12 days of flute playing; cymbal used alone; minor Levites as cadets; minimum 12 Levites on platform; debate on their status

name: Flute Playing in the Temple (Chalil)
notes: 12 days per year for flute before altar: Pesach slaughtering, second Pesach, first day of Pesach, Shavuot, 8 days of Sukkot; reed flute preferred over copper; concluding with single flute

name: Redemption of Ancestral Field During Jubilee Period
notes: Cannot consecrate less than 2 years before Jubilee; cannot redeem less than 1 year after Jubilee; counting months for Temple treasury; what happens if not redeemed; priests entering the field; Rabbi Eliezer's view of abandoned field

name: Sale of Field with Jubilee Provisions
notes: Cannot redeem within first two years; blight/shemitah years don't count; resale price calculation; prohibition on selling distant field to redeem nearby; incremental redemption; comparison to Temple treasury redemption

name: Hillel's Enactment for Walled City House Redemption
notes: Buyer's concealment to prevent redemption; Hillel's enactment that seller deposits money in court chamber and breaks down the door; procedural reform

name: Defamer's Fine (Motzi Shem Ra) — 100 Sela
notes: 100 sela fixed fine regardless of woman's status; compared to rapist/seducer 50 sela; lesson that speech-based sin is graver than action; connection to spies narrative

name: Vow of One's Weight (Mishkal)
notes: Vowing to donate one's weight in silver or gold; incident of Yirmatya's mother; how to measure weight of a limb; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosi on displacement method

name: Court Coercion to Bring Voluntary Offering
notes: Court repossesses property of those obligated in burnt offerings and peace offerings; coercion until person says 'I want to'; parallel to coerced get; distinction from sin and guilt offerings
